desc: Ideation: subset enumeration (target ≤ 4), cost via LCM; identified pitfall that naive subset DP can illegally reuse the same nums element for two blocks.
Fix: prove top-4 cheapest distinct elements per subset suffice (exchange argument: ≤4 blocks, so an unused top-4 element can replace any outside choice without increasing cost).

Implement solution: lcm[mask] via gcd; cost(x,mask)=ceil to multiple; collect candidate set (≤60 indices); DP over candidates with submask transitions (each element used at most once); return dp[full].
Verify on the three examples plus counterexample nums=[6,101], target=[4,9] (expect 6) and zero-cost case; confirm complexity O(15·n + 60·3^4) fits constraints.
Deliver final code in starter format with imports (List, gcd, nsmallest) and brief comments explaining the distinct-element fix.
